author: Diptanu Choudhury
text: We are seeing backlash against sandboxes for primarily a couple of reasons - vendors don't support users to overcommit compute. You can't pay for N cores and overcommit the number of sandboxes that are run on those cores. In reality agents don't uniformly use resources during [quoting @arlanr: 'Turning the entire web into a filesystem. Code hallucinations are not a model problem. They're a data problem. Every day, APIs ship breaking changes, deprecate endpoints, and rename parameters.']
suggestedEngagement: Affirm the overcommit point from a scheduling angle — ask if they're considering work-stealing or bursty reservation models like Nomad's
Challenge or probe the data problem framing: ask whether dynamic API fetching at inference time is viable or if there's a better approach for agent tooling
Share perspective on sandbox adoption blockers from a consultancy angle: pricing models vs. technical trust, which is the bigger blocker?
discoveryMethod: Found on Following feed (profile scroll), 1st scroll — post from 2 hours ago
